transcript.content: Hello, I’m Dr. ____. What brings you in today?

Hello, Doctor. Well, I came in today because... I keep doing these odd things down at the church. 

Like, I'll be standing by the potluck table, and I'll just be holding the serving spoon up in the air and... just not moving at all. Or I'll find myself folding the exact same stack of napkins over and over again, even with people waiting on me in line. I just wanted to see someone about it, because it's not right.
Do you ever hear or see things that other people don’t?
No, I don't. I mean, my hearing isn't quite what it used to be at my age, but... no, I've never heard voices or seen things that aren't really there. I haven't noticed anything like that at all.
Do you feel a strong urge to do these repeated actions to relieve anxiety or prevent something bad from happening?

No, it's not like that at all. I don't feel worried or... or like I'm trying to stop something bad from happening. Honestly, I don't even really feel an urge to do it. It's more like I just sort of get stuck doing it, or I just freeze up, and I don't really know why.
Do you ever find yourself unable to move or speak even when you want to?

Well, no, I don't think it's exactly like that. It's not like I'm trying to say something or trying to walk away and my body just won't let me. I don't feel trapped or anything. 

It's more like... I just don't move. I don't really have the thought that I want to move or speak right then. I just sort of stay still for a bit until it passes.
When you’re like that, do your arms or legs ever stay in whatever position someone puts them in, even if it’s an awkward position?

No, I don't think so. Honestly, nobody has ever tried to move my arms or legs around when I get quiet like that. So I wouldn't really know for sure, but... no, I haven't noticed anything like that happening.
Have you been finding yourself much less interested in other people or activities than you used to be?

No, I wouldn't say that. I still do my regular things, and I like seeing folks just as much as I always have. I haven't noticed any... any drop in my interest or anything like that. I just go about my day same as usual.
When you are standing still like that, do you feel aware of what is happening around you?

Oh, yes, I'm fully aware. I hear and see everything just fine. I don't... I don't blank out or lose my senses or anything like that. I can hear if the television is on, or if somebody is walking by. I'm just standing quiet for a spell, that's all.
When you are standing still like that, do your arms or legs ever stay in an unusual position if someone places them there?

Like I said just a minute ago, doctor, nobody has ever tried moving my arms or legs around when I'm standing like that. So I really couldn't tell you if they'd stay in a strange position or not. I just stand there on my own.
When you get like that, has anyone ever moved your arm or leg and it stayed in that position, almost as if it were set there?

Well, like I just said, doctor... no one has ever tried doing that to me. I don't have folks coming up and moving my limbs around when I'm standing there. So I really couldn't say if they'd stay put like that or not. I just keep them where I put them myself.
When someone gently moves your arm or leg, does it tend to stay where they put it for a while, almost like it becomes set in that position?

Doctor, I... I feel like we're going in circles here. Like I told you, nobody has ever tried to move my arms or legs when I'm just standing quiet. So I really don't know if they would stay put or not. It's just not something that happens.
During those times when you stand still, has anyone ever gently moved one of your arms, and did it stay in that new position?
Doctor, I really don't know how else to say this... you keep asking me the same thing. No, nobody has ever moved my arm or leg when I'm standing there. So I don't know what would happen.
If I ask you to do something simple like lift your arm or open your hand, do you ever find yourself doing it automatically even if you don’t mean to?
No, I don't think so. When I move my arm or open my hand, it's because I want to. I don't just do things without meaning to.
When someone gently moves one of your arms, does it stay in that new position for a while?
Doctor, we... we just went over this. Like I said before, nobody has ever tried to move my arm when I'm standing still. I really don't have an answer for you because it's just never happened.
When someone places your arm in a certain position, does it stay there instead of dropping back down?

Doctor, I'm... I'm getting a little frustrated here. You keep asking me the exact same thing about my arms. Like I've said twice now, nobody has done that. Nobody moves my arms around, so I just don't know if they would stay up or fall down. It just hasn't happened.
Have you ever felt as if someone else was controlling your thoughts or actions?
No, I haven't. My thoughts are my own, and I do what I want to do. Nobody else is controlling me.
When someone gently moves your arm, does it stay in that new position for a while?

Doctor, I don't understand why we keep going back to my arms. You've asked me this a few times now. Like I keep saying, nobody comes up and moves my arms around for me. I really don't have a different answer to give you because it just hasn't ever happened.
If I gently place your arm in a position, does it stay there for a while even after I let go?

Doctor, are you... are you listening to me? You just asked me that exact same thing about my arm again. I really don't know what else to tell you. Like I just said, nobody does that to me, so I don't know what my arm would do. I guess if you want to try it right now you can, but I just don't have a different answer for you.
If I gently place your arm in a certain position, does it stay there for a while after I let go?

Doctor, I... I really don't understand what's going on here. You just asked me that for the third time in a row. 

No, it wouldn't stay there. If you moved my arm and then let go, I'd just put it right back down in my lap. I just... I don't have a different answer for you, no matter how many times you ask it.
When you’re like that and standing very still, do you feel unable to move even if you try?

Well, I don't really know what you mean by being "like that." I don't just stand around frozen. If I'm standing still, it's just because I'm resting or waiting on something, and I can always move whenever I want to. I've never felt stuck or unable to move my own body.
Have you had any periods where you barely moved or spoke at all for hours or longer?

No, I haven't had anything like that happen. I mean, I might sit in my chair and rest for a good bit, maybe watch a little TV, but I'm not just... frozen. I talk just fine. If the phone rings or somebody asks me something, I answer them. I've never had a time where I just sat there for hours without moving or saying a word.
